claims.statement: Wurzel and Hsu, arXiv 2105.10954 v4: the ideal 0-D power balance P_c >= P_B (eqs 6-8, 16, 22, 41, D1-D5) with P_c = f_c n1 n2 <sigma v> E and P_B = C_B n_e^2 sqrt(T_e) gamma(Z_eff), C_B = 5.34e-37 W m^3 keV^(-1/2); gamma = Z_eff (1 + 1.78 t^1.34) + 2.12 t (1 + 1.1 t + t^2 - 1.25 t^2.5), t = T_e/(m_e c^2) (eq. D2); optimal proton-boron mix x = n_B/n_i = 1/6, Z_eff = 3 (eqs D3-D4, footnote 138); Table II/III list '-' for p-11B; Fig. 28 caption 'P_B always exceeds P_c when T_e >~ T_i/3', using the parameterized Nevins-Swain reactivity.

Wang, Li, Wu, Cui, arXiv 2601.00241 v1 (Jan 2026), eqs (1)-(6) and Table I: an updated p-11B S-factor (segments E<=0.4, 0.4-0.7, 0.7-10 MeV; the first reprints the Nevins-Swain coefficients) and the reactivity as the Maxwellian integral; Fig. 8 text 'if electron-ion thermal equilibrium is assumed (T_e = T), the resulting bremsstrahlung loss ... exceeds the fusion power density over the entire temperature range' (with Rider's bremsstrahlung). Ochs and Fisch, arXiv 2310.18508 v1, eq. (14): the same relativistic bremsstrahlung bracket (prefactor 7.56e-11 eV cm^3/s, x^2 term).

The Bosch-Hale (1992) D-T reactivity coefficients and the Nevins-Swain (2000) p-11B high-temperature reactivity coefficients P1-P7 (valid 50-500 keV) are the values transcribed from the Wurzel-Hsu public code (github.com/swurzel/lawson-criterion-paper, MIT licence, commit 4ae563bf, dated after the 2022 paper), the preregistered fallback. NEITHER the producer NOR the independent auditor could obtain Bosch-Hale 1992 or Nevins-Swain 2000. These coefficients are NOT verified against the primary papers. Only indirect checks exist: the NS low-energy S-factor block agrees with Wang Table I; the transcribed NS fit is 0.985-0.996 of the Maxwellian integral of the NS S-factor at 50-200 keV, 0.976 and 0.965 at 250 and 300 keV, 0.940 at 400 keV, 0.917 at 500 keV (reproduced by the auditor, Tier X); the auditor's recollection of Bosch-Hale agrees (memory, not a pinned source).

Method (Arb ball arithmetic, python-flint 0.6.0, 128 bit; every coefficient a decimal string from fits.json): certified Maxwellian reactivity of a cross-section fit by rigorous acb.integral plus the temperature-interval bound sv(a)(a/b)^(3/2) <= sv(T) <= sv(b)(b/a)^(3/2) (valid because the S-factor is certified >= 0); best-first branch and bound with outward rounding for max P_c/P_B over (T_i, x) boxes; bisection plus a certified witness for theta*; the reduction from the face theta_hi to every theta in [theta_hi, 1] uses that P_B increases with T_e for T_e <= 500 keV < m_e c^2, whose electron-electron term derivative is positive by PBI-A-0001 (the step 'positive derivative implies monotone' is not formalised). Not replayed in Lean.

D-T positive control against Wurzel-Hsu, passed for the model the authors' code ran (the gate model was chosen after a float run, Deviation 6): certified ideal-ignition temperature [4.2989514, 4.2989523] keV (printed 4.3); argmin of n T tau_E at Q = infinity in [14.128, 14.442] keV (printed 14), minimum [2.94410, 2.94502]e21 (printed 2.9e21); argmin of n tau_E in [25.590, 26.212] keV (printed 26), minimum [1.55227, 1.55279]e20 (printed 1.6e20); constant hull T_ign [4.2608, 4.3468], TP min [2.94400, 2.96351]e21. Other certified readings: parameterized non-relativistic, text C_B/J, f_c = 0.2: T_ign [4.29959, 4.29959], TP min [2.94923, 2.95056]e21 (straddles the 2.95 rounding edge); parameterized relativistic, code constants: T_ign [4.32619, 4.32620], TP min [2.96275, 2.96409]e21 (prints 3.0); integrated non-relativistic, text C_B/J, f_c = 0.2: TP min [2.93077, 2.93168]e21 (prints 2.9). These 'text' variants use f_c = 0.2 from the code, not the text's 3.5/17.6 (audit correction C1). Every variant gives 4.3, 14, 26 and 1.6e20; only the second digit of the Table III minimum depends on the reading.

At T_e = T_i, on T_i in [50, 500] keV and boron fraction x in [0.05, 0.5], P_c < P_B everywhere (no ideal-ignition window) for both reactivity fits, in this ideal 0-D model: certified max P_c/P_B in [0.42139, 0.42556] (Nevins-Swain, argmax about 202 keV, x = 0.100) and [0.42869, 0.43260] (Wang, about 208.5 keV, x = 0.101); at the Wurzel-Hsu mix x = 1/6: [0.39016, 0.39240] (NS) and [0.39732, 0.40083] (Wang). Certified reactivity multiplier m* in [2.350, 2.373] (NS) and [2.312, 2.333] (Wang): any reactivity at most 2.349 x NS on [50, 500] keV gives P_c < P_B on the whole box. The maximum is interior; widening the box (x to [0.005, 0.95], T_i to [20, 1000] keV) leaves it unchanged (auditor, float, Tier X). Not replayed in Lean.

A window needs T_e/T_i below a threshold theta*, certified only for theta in [theta_hi, 1]: Nevins-Swain full box [0.4223, 0.4308] (witness at theta = 0.4223: T_i = 243.5 keV, x = 0.0922, R >= 1.0077); NS x = 1/6 [0.3753, 0.3828] (witness 243.5 keV, R >= 1.0082); Wang full box [0.4381, 0.4470] (witness R >= 1.0082 at 243.5 keV, x = 0.092); Wang x = 1/6 [0.396, 0.402] (explicit theta scan: at theta = 0.402 certified max R <= 0.99995; at theta = 0.396 a witness at T_i = 261.65 keV, x = 1/6 with R >= 1.00037, a thin margin; audit C8). Above theta_hi the face argument of PBI-C-0001 applies. These thresholds hold for these two fits and Putvinski's bremsstrahlung only; they scale with the reactivity (PBI-X-0001). The ideal 0-D model has no synchrotron, no transport, no ion-electron coupling, no alpha heating of electrons, no ash, Maxwellian only; the maximum interior is about 202 keV and x about 0.10 at theta = 1.

Controls, run with the gate before the p-11B headline: P1 D-T reproduction passes (G1, G2, G2b, G3, G4 true, for the authors' code model); N1 reactivity x 0.5 FAILS the gate (T_ign 5.3724 keV, TP min 6.285e21, LP min 3.230e20); N2 bremsstrahlung removed FAILS (no ignition temperature; the p-11B ratio becomes infinite and the 'no window' conclusion flips); N3 Lean controls fail (PBI-A-0002); S-factor positivity certified. Audit correction C6: the D-T gate G3 does NOT discriminate for the p-11B conclusion (it passes under N1, since halving the reactivity only strengthens an exclusion). The p-11B pipeline's ability to find a window is shown instead by the theta* witnesses (R > 1 at theta_lo), the theta = 1/3 check (R = 1.113 NS, 1.161 Wang; Tier X) and N2. The auditor read the recorded check vectors of N1 and N2 in logs/certify.json; the gate code was not re-run by the auditor.

Independent AI audit (AUDIT.md, a separate agent instance, ACCEPT_WITH_CORRECTIONS, not a person): with its own mpmath.iv code (different method: 11,513 x 4,500 geometric/uniform cell grid with corner monotonicity bounds) it reproduced rigorously the D-T T_ign for three readings, the NS max P_c/P_B over the box [0.42140, 0.42470] and at x = 1/6 [0.39016, 0.39311], the NS theta* upper side (U < 1 at 0.43125 and 0.38281), and re-evaluated the producer's NS witnesses (R in [1.0077322, 1.0077331] and [1.0082393, 1.0082399]). Every producer enclosure contains the auditor's value. The Wang-side numbers and the D-T TP/LP minimisers of the gate model are float only on the auditor's side (Tier X). The auditor did not re-run the producer's Arb integrals.

HEADLINE. In an ideal 0-D power-balance model (Wurzel-Hsu's, with Putvinski's bremsstrahlung), with two reactivity fits (Nevins-Swain as transcribed from the Wurzel-Hsu code, and Wang et al. 2026), in the box T_i in [50, 500] keV, x in [0.05, 0.5]: there is no ignition window at T_e = T_i (certified max P_c/P_B [0.4214, 0.4256] NS, [0.4287, 0.4326] Wang), and a window needs T_e/T_i below thresholds theta* of about 0.42-0.45 (full box) or 0.375-0.402 (x = 1/6), certified only for theta <= 1, for these fits and this bremsstrahlung only. Tier C (Arb ball arithmetic, not replayed in Lean; coefficients not verified against primary papers). Concerns the model and the fits only: nothing about any device, reactor, feasibility or economics.

Float checks (Tier X, supporting nothing by themselves): the producer's independent float implementation (scipy) is inside every certified enclosure (theta_c,max 0.4286 NS box, 0.3811 NS x = 1/6, 0.4451 Wang box, 0.3988 Wang x = 1/6; max R at theta = 1 0.4232 NS, 0.4309 Wang); the Wurzel-Hsu Fig. 28 remark: at T_e = T_i/3 and x = 1/6 max P_c/P_B = 1.113 (NS, T_i about 248 keV) and 1.161 (Wang, about 268.5 keV), so the certified threshold 0.375-0.383 lies above 1/3; the NS fit versus the Maxwellian integral of the NS S-factor (0.985 at 50 keV down to 0.917 at 500 keV); the auditor's float sensitivities: reactivity x1.1/1.2/1.32 moves theta_c to 0.477/0.524/0.579, Rider's bremsstrahlung moves it by about +1%; the auditor's pure-text D-T row (f_c = 3.5/17.6, parameterized non-relativistic, text C_B and 1.6e-16 J/keV): T_ign in [4.3071225, 4.3071227] keV and n T tau_E >= 2.95e21 with a value 2.96846e21 at 14.2486 keV, so the minimum lies in [2.95e21, 2.96846e21] and prints 3.0e21 (auditor mpmath.iv, scratch not shipped; the producer has not certified this row with its own pipeline); Wang/NS reactivity ratio 1.016, 1.000, 1.005, 1.016, 1.070, 1.154, 1.262 at 50, 100, 150, 200, 300, 400, 500 keV.
